summary: OpenTelemetry trace context leaks between workflows when worker threads/fibers are reused because Context.attach() is called but Context.detach() is not always called, allowing trace context to persist across unrelated workflow executions.
userImpact: Users utilizing OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing observe incorrect traces with spans from unrelated workflows mixed together, breaking observability and monitoring capabilities.
rootCause: OpenTelemetry context is attached using Context.attach() but the corresponding Context.detach(token) is not always called, allowing the context to remain active and be reused by subsequent workflow/activity executions when worker threads/fibers are reused.
proposedFix: Ensure Context.detach(token) is called after Context.attach() to properly clean up and detach OpenTelemetry context following the OTeL specification for context lifecycle management.
keyQuote: Activities from those untraced workflows may end up generating spans and being attached to the trace of a previously executed workflow.
